common_name: Pusa Purple Cluster Brinjal (IARI Early Cluster-Fruited Indian Eggplant)

planting.note: Start indoors 8 weeks before last frost and transplant into warm soil once nights stay reliably above 55°F, since this variety is grown for both spring and monsoon-season crops in its native India.

directions: Released by the Indian Agricultural Research Institute, Pusa Purple Cluster is an early-maturing brinjal prized for bearing its small, dark purple, medium-long fruits in dense clusters of four to nine rather than singly, giving a notably concentrated harvest per picking. Plants show good tolerance to bacterial wilt, making this a reliable choice in warm, humid growing conditions where that disease limits other brinjal varieties. Begin picking as soon as fruits reach a glossy, firm stage, since frequent cluster harvesting keeps plants setting new flushes through a long warm season. Its compact, heavy-bearing habit suits both home gardens and market growing in regions with an extended frost-free period.

common_name: Arka Nidhi Brinjal (IIHR Bacterial Wilt-Resistant Indian Eggplant)

planting.note: Start indoors 8 weeks before last frost and transplant into warm, well-drained soil once nights stay reliably above 55°F; this is a long-season variety best suited to climates with an extended warm growing period.

directions: Developed by the Indian Institute of Horticultural Research (IIHR) in Bangalore from a cross of Dingras Multiple Purple and Arka Sheel, Arka Nidhi is a tall, well-branched brinjal bred for resistance to bacterial wilt, a disease that devastates many eggplant plantings in warm, humid regions. Its medium-long fruits have glossy blue-black-purple skin and a green-purple calyx, borne in clusters across two main flushes of production, with tender flesh whose seeds mature slowly, keeping bitterness low even in larger fruit. The dark purple young stems and purple-veined foliage make the plants easy to distinguish in a mixed vegetable bed. Because it is a longer-season type, give it the fullest possible warm window and consistent moisture to reach its full, heavy-bearing potential.

common_name: Violetta Lunga di Napoli Eggplant (Neapolitan Heirloom Long Purple Eggplant)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant out only once nights stay reliably above 55°F in rich, well-drained soil.

directions: A traditional heirloom from the Naples region of southern Italy, Violetta Lunga di Napoli produces smooth, cylindrical, deep purple fruits reaching roughly 8 inches long on early-bearing, prolific plants. The flesh is notably mild and nearly seedless, with a sweet, nutty flavor that distinguishes it from larger, seedier eggplant types, making it a favorite sliced into rounds for grilling, baking, or sautéing. Stake plants once fruit begins to set heavily, since the slender fruiting habit can bend stems under a full crop. Pick fruit while the skin is still taut and glossy for the best texture and to encourage continued flowering.

common_name: Tsakoniki Eggplant (Leonidio PDO Greek Heirloom White-Striped Eggplant)

planting.note: Start indoors 6-8 weeks before the last frost and transplant into warm, well-drained soil once nights stay reliably above 55°F.

directions: Tsakoniki is a slender heirloom eggplant traditionally grown around Leonidio in the Tsakonia region of the Greek Peloponnese, where it holds European Protected Designation of Origin status. Fruits are thin and elongated with a pointed end, their purple skin softened by pale white streaks, and the flesh is notably sweet and tender with little of the bitterness common to larger eggplant types. Local growers traditionally raise it on sandy, terraced plots near the coast, but it adapts well to any warm, well-drained garden bed with full sun. Harvest fruits while still slender and glossy for the mildest flavor, and pick regularly to keep plants setting new fruit through the season.
sources: Slow Food Foundation for Biodiversity (Ark of Taste)

common_name: Surati Ravaiya Brinjal (Gujarati Heirloom Round Stuffing Eggplant)

planting.note: Start indoors 8 weeks before last frost and transplant into warm, fertile soil once nights stay reliably above 55°F.

directions: Surati Ravaiya is a traditional landrace brinjal from the Surat area of south Gujarat, grown for its round, glossy purple fruits that typically reach a substantial 150 to 200 grams each. Its tender, mild flesh and sturdy round shape make it the classic choice for bharela ravaiya, the popular Gujarati dish of baby eggplants stuffed with a spiced peanut-and-coconut masala and simmered in sauce. Plants show useful field tolerance to shoot and fruit borer as well as little leaf disease, both common regional pests, but fruit set can be uneven during heavy monsoon rains, so good drainage helps steady production. Harvest fruits while still firm and glossy for the best texture in stuffed preparations.
